science.qualification: Photosphere color from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum, dimmed and reddened toward the limb by the quadratic laws Claret, Hauschildt & Witte (2012) compute from PHOENIX model atmospheres at 2,566 K and log g 5.2396: their R band for the red channel, V for green and B for blue. The disc is unresolved: the limb is a model, not an image or a measured profile. Self-luminous, so no lighting.

science.label: Campaign 12
science.description: Brightness of the star's surface that reproduces its light as it turns once in 3.3 days, fitted with starry to the star's EVEREST light curve of K2 campaign 12, which its authors make from the K2 mission's pixels (its flux, with lightkurve's default quality mask) (the light varies by 1.5%; the map's curve leaves a scatter of 2.0%, the light's own noise being 1.7%). A light curve fixes how bright each longitude is, not the latitude of what darkens it. Luger et al. (2017, Nature Astronomy 1, 0129) give the star's rotation in their text (Methods, the paragraph that establishes the rotation period and the flare rate: "The rotation period is determined to be 3.30 ± 0.14 d."): a rotation period of 3.30 ± 0.14 d. The rotation and its period are theirs, taken as published; no criteria were applied to them here. The map is made at the tilt the page draws the star with, 90°. Gaia DR3 lists no other star within 16 arcseconds of it. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · brightness map made here · Campaign 12

science.label: Color + brightness
science.description: The star's color (#ffcd6a, its Color dataset) over the brightness map this project made from the star's light in K2 campaign 12 (December 2016 to March 2017): the map's scale, 97.5% to 102.5% of the mean surface, runs from a darker, richer tone of the same hue to the color itself. The contrast is drawn far stronger than it is, so the parts can be told apart: the darkest part gives 4.9% less light than the brightest. Longitudes are fixed by the light curve; latitudes and shapes are not. No color change of the spots is drawn: none is measured. A reduction made in this project, not a published map.
science.title: K2 · the star in its color over its brightness map · December 2016 to March 2017

limbMaterial.composition: a colored plate over the Gaia-colored sphere: its alpha darkens the channel the Claret, Hauschildt & Witte (2012) model laws darken most, and its color holds the other two at their own laws; transparent outside the silhouette
